diff --git a/tests/unit/llms/chatgpt/test_chatgpt_reasoning_model_info.py b/tests/unit/llms/chatgpt/test_chatgpt_reasoning_model_info.py
new file mode 100644
index 0000000000..69ed8041b5
--- /dev/null
+++ b/tests/unit/llms/chatgpt/test_chatgpt_reasoning_model_info.py
@@ -0,0 +1,96 @@
+"""
+The chatgpt/ spellings of OpenAI models must advertise the same reasoning
+capabilities as their openai twins, since /model/info reads them straight off
+the entry and clients gate their effort controls on them.
+
+The one intended divergence is max on gpt-5.6: the ChatGPT backend serves these
+models over the Responses API, which accepts it, while the openai chat-mode
+entries must not advertise it because /v1/chat/completions refuses it.
+"""
+
+from collections.abc import Generator
+
+import pytest
+
+import litellm
+
+_REASONING_KEYS = (
+    "supports_reasoning",
+    "supports_none_reasoning_effort",
+    "supports_minimal_reasoning_effort",
+    "supports_low_reasoning_effort",
+    "supports_xhigh_reasoning_effort",
+    "default_reasoning_effort",
+)
+
+_CHATGPT_MODELS_WITH_OPENAI_TWIN = (
+    "gpt-5.1-codex-max",
+    "gpt-5.1-codex-mini",
+    "gpt-5.2",
+    "gpt-5.2-codex",
+    "gpt-5.3-chat-latest",
+    "gpt-5.3-codex",
+    "gpt-5.4",
+    "gpt-5.4-pro",
+    "gpt-5.5",
+    "gpt-5.6-luna",
+    "gpt-5.6-sol",
+    "gpt-5.6-terra",
+)
+
+
+@pytest.fixture
+def local_model_cost_map(monkeypatch: pytest.MonkeyPatch) -> Generator[None, None, None]:
+    monkeypatch.setenv("LITELLM_LOCAL_MODEL_COST_MAP", "True")
+    monkeypatch.setattr(litellm, "model_cost", litellm.get_model_cost_map(url=""))
+    litellm.get_model_info.cache_clear()
+    yield
+    litellm.get_model_info.cache_clear()
+
+
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("model", _CHATGPT_MODELS_WITH_OPENAI_TWIN)
+def test_chatgpt_model_info_matches_openai_twin_reasoning_flags(model: str, local_model_cost_map: None) -> None:
+    chatgpt_info = litellm.get_model_info(model=f"chatgpt/{model}")
+    openai_info = litellm.get_model_info(model=model, custom_llm_provider="openai")
+
+    assert chatgpt_info["supports_reasoning"] is True
+    for key in _REASONING_KEYS:
+        assert chatgpt_info.get(key) == openai_info.get(key), key
+
+
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("model", ("chatgpt/gpt-5.3-codex-spark", "chatgpt/gpt-5.3-instant"))
+def test_chatgpt_models_without_openai_twin_declare_reasoning(model: str, local_model_cost_map: None) -> None:
+    assert litellm.get_model_info(model=model)["supports_reasoning"] is True
+
+
+def test_every_chatgpt_entry_declares_reasoning(local_model_cost_map: None) -> None:
+    missing = [
+        key
+        for key, entry in litellm.model_cost.items()
+        if key.startswith("chatgpt/") and entry.get("supports_reasoning") is not True
+    ]
+    assert missing == []
+
+
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("model", ("chatgpt/gpt-5.6-sol", "chatgpt/gpt-5.6-terra", "chatgpt/gpt-5.6-luna"))
+def test_chatgpt_gpt_5_6_model_info_advertises_full_effort_range(model: str, local_model_cost_map: None) -> None:
+    info = litellm.get_model_info(model=model)
+
+    assert info["supports_reasoning"] is True
+    assert info["supports_none_reasoning_effort"] is True
+    assert info["supports_minimal_reasoning_effort"] is False
+    assert info["supports_xhigh_reasoning_effort"] is True
+    assert info["supports_max_reasoning_effort"] is True
+
+
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("model", ("chatgpt/gpt-5.6-sol", "chatgpt/gpt-5.6-terra", "chatgpt/gpt-5.6-luna"))
+def test_chatgpt_gpt_5_6_deployment_advertises_max_effort(model: str, local_model_cost_map: None) -> None:
+    from litellm.router_utils.reasoning_effort_capability import resolve_supported_reasoning_efforts
+
+    resolved = resolve_supported_reasoning_efforts(litellm.get_model_info(model=model), deployment_is_mapped=True)
+
+    assert resolved is not None
+    assert "max" in resolved
+    assert "xhigh" in resolved
+    assert "none" in resolved
+    assert "minimal" not in resolved

title: [Bug]: LiteLLM Proxy 1.100.0 serializes image-edit uploads as strings for OpenAI GPT Image models

judge.reasoning: Both patches address the same root cause: `_read_request_body` re-parses the multipart body, so the `image[]`/`mask[]` parts survive in `data` as raw UploadFiles alongside the converted `image`/`mask` buffers, and the SDK stringifies them into text parts. Both independent tests pass for both patches. Patch A drops exactly the two bracketed keys; Patch B drops any UploadFile under the four known file keys and converts any other leaked UploadFile to BytesIO rather than letting it be stringified. B's approach is keyed on the actual failure condition (a raw UploadFile in the forwarded payload) rather than on two literal key names, so it is more robust at low risk; the extra conversion for unknown upload fields is out of scope but adds no risk and is tested. On tests, B is clearly stronger: beyond unit checks on the captured dict, it adds an end-to-end regression that drives `litellm.aimage_edit` through an httpx MockTransport and asserts the real multipart body contains a filename-bearing file part with the PNG bytes and no `UploadFile(`/`BytesIO` text, which mirrors the issue precisely. A's tests are adequate but only inspect the captured dict. On scope, A includes unrelated reformatting of existing test lines (the 8 removed lines), which is churn; B touches only what it needs. Craft is comparable; B's comment explains why the filtering exists, and its `StarletteUploadFile` annotation is correct since FastAPI's UploadFile subclasses it. B is the better fix.

issue_md:
### Check for existing issues

- [x] I have searched the existing issues and checked that my issue is not a duplicate.

### What happened?

Image edits through the LiteLLM Proxy fail in version 1.100.0 for OpenAI GPT Image models. The uploaded image file is being converted to a string representation of a Python `BytesIO` object (`"<_io.BytesIO object at 0x7f0d0bc73600>"`) before being sent to OpenAI.

OpenAI rejects this with:
```json
{
  "error": {
    "message": "Invalid type for 'image[0]': expected a file, but got a string instead.",
    "type": "invalid_request_error",
    "param": "image[0]",
    "code": "invalid_type"
  }
}
```

The same request succeeds in LiteLLM version 1.95.0.

### User Flow

Before a fix: A user sends an image-edit request through LiteLLM Proxy 1.100.0 using a multipart/form-data request to POST /v1/images/edits with an uploaded image file and a prompt (e.g., "Make this image photorealistic"). LiteLLM receives the UploadFile correctly but serializes it to a string before forwarding to OpenAI. OpenAI rejects the request because it expects a file object, not a string representation.

1. User sends: `curl -X POST "http://localhost:4000/v1/images/edits" -F "model=openai/gpt-image-2" -F "prompt=Make this image photorealistic" -F "image[]=@./input.png;type=image/png"`
2. LiteLLM receives UploadFile with filename, size, and content-type headers
3. LiteLLM converts the UploadFile's BytesIO object to a string
4. LiteLLM forwards stringified image to OpenAI
5. OpenAI rejects with invalid_type error

After a fix: The same user flow succeeds. LiteLLM preserves the UploadFile/BytesIO object and forwards it to OpenAI as a multipart file, and OpenAI processes it successfully.

### Proof the bug occurs

Config / setup the proxy ran with:
Default LiteLLM Proxy setup with OpenAI API key configured

Version or commit:
1.100.0 (regression; works in 1.95.0)

Commands and their full output:

title: [Bug]: Fix "vertex_ai/xai/grok-4.6" entry in "model_prices_and_context_window.json" — missing supports_prompt_caching

judge.reasoning: Both diffs touch only the pre-existing test file; the cost-map JSON edits (the actual fix to model_prices_and_context_window.json and the backup) were evidently stripped as generated files from both, so the comparison rests on the test changes. Patch A mostly reshuffles the existing tests: it swaps the supports_prompt_caching() check for a get_model_info() lookup (making the first test redundant with the second), adds Final annotations on locals, and adds a couple of cache_read_input_token_cost assertions that were already implied by the filter. It adds no coverage of the backup file, which the issue explicitly calls out. Patch B leaves the existing tests intact and adds a parametrized test that reads both model_prices_and_context_window.json and litellm/model_prices_and_context_window_backup.json directly from disk and asserts every vertex_ai/xai/grok-* row with a cache-read price sets supports_prompt_caching: true. That test would fail before the fix and pass after, and it is the only one that guards the backup-file requirement and prevents the two files from drifting. Path resolution (parents[2] from tests/test_litellm/) is correct. Using pydantic TypeAdapter to parse JSON is slightly unconventional but harmless. B adds real, issue-targeted test value; A is largely churn.

### Check for existing issues

- [x] I have searched the existing issues and checked that my issue is not a duplicate.

### What happened?

https://github.com/BerriAI/litellm/blob/v1.102.0-rc.1/model_prices_and_context_window.json#L48398-L48416

This entry has `cache_read_input_token_cost` (5e-07) and `cache_read_input_token_cost_above_200k_tokens` (1e-06) but no `supports_prompt_caching`, so `supports_prompt_caching()` returns false and `GET /v1/model/info` reports `"supports_prompt_caching": false` for a Vertex Grok 4.6 deployment.

The same model on the other providers does set it:

- `xai/grok-4.6` → `supports_prompt_caching: true` (L49979)
- `azure_ai/grok-4.6` → `supports_prompt_caching: true`

xAI prompt caching is provider-managed (automatic on a stable prefix), and the Vertex route does return `usage.prompt_tokens_details.cached_tokens` > 0 on follow-up turns, which is what the cache-read rate on this entry bills. Callers that gate on `/model/info` before reusing a prefix therefore skip caching on the Vertex route only.

The whole `vertex_ai/xai/grok-*` family looks the same — each has a cache-read price and none sets the flag:

| key | cache_read_input_token_cost | supports_prompt_caching |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `vertex_ai/xai/grok-4.1-fast-non-reasoning` | 5e-08 | absent |
| `vertex_ai/xai/grok-4.1-fast-reasoning` | 5e-08 | absent |
| `vertex_ai/xai/grok-4.20-non-reasoning` | 2e-07 | absent |
| `vertex_ai/xai/grok-4.20-reasoning` | 2e-07 | absent |
| `vertex_ai/xai/grok-4.3` | 2e-07 | absent |
| `vertex_ai/xai/grok-4.6` | 5e-07 | absent |

We also need to update [model_prices_and_context_window_backup.json](https://github.com/BerriAI/litellm/blob/v1.102.0-rc.1/litellm/model_prices_and_context_window_backup.json).

Confirmed on `v1.102.0-rc.1` and current `main`.

### User Flow

**Before a (hypothetical) fix**

The flow fails when I ask the gateway whether Vertex Grok 4.6 supports prompt caching: the catalog says no, even though a follow-up completion on that same model returns cached tokens.

1. I start the proxy with a config that exposes `grok-4.6-vertex` (`vertex_ai/xai/grok-4.6`) and `grok-4.6-direct` (`xai/grok-4.6`) and see it listening on `http://localhost:4000`.
2. I send `GET http://localhost:4000/v1/models` with `Authorization: Bearer sk-[REDACTED]`. I get HTTP 200 and both model names in `data`.
3. I send `GET http://localhost:4000/v1/model/info` with the same header. I get HTTP 200. For `grok-4.6-vertex`, `model_info.supports_prompt_caching` is `false` (or absent) while `cache_read_input_token_cost` is `5e-07`. For `grok-4.6-direct`, `supports_prompt_caching` is `true`.
4. I send `POST http://localhost:4000/v1/chat/completions` for `grok-4.6-vertex` with a long stable system prefix, a first user turn, and header `x-grok-conv-id: conv_repro_1`. I get HTTP 200 and `usage.prompt_tokens_details.cached_tokens` of `0`.
5. I send the same URL again with the same `x-grok-conv-id`, appending the assistant reply and a follow-up user turn. I get HTTP 200 and `usage.prompt_tokens_details.cached_tokens` greater than `0`.
6. I send `POST http://localhost:4000/v1/responses` for `grok-4.6-vertex` with the same prefix and `"prompt_cache_key": "conv_repro_1"`. I get HTTP 200 and `usage.input_tokens_details.cached_tokens` of `0`.
7. I send the same URL again with the same `prompt_cache_key` and the follow-up turn. I get HTTP 200 and `usage.input_tokens_details.cached_tokens` greater than `0`.

**After a (hypothetical) fix**

The flow succeeds at the catalog check: Vertex Grok 4.6 is listed as supporting prompt caching, matching the live cache hits on the next turns.

1. I start the proxy with a config that exposes `grok-4.6-vertex` (`vertex_ai/xai/grok-4.6`) and `grok-4.6-direct` (`xai/grok-4.6`) and see it listening on `http://localhost:4000`.
2. I send `GET http://localhost:4000/v1/models` with `Authorization: Bearer sk-[REDACTED]`. I get HTTP 200 and both model names in `data`.
3. I send `GET http://localhost:4000/v1/model/info` with the same header. I get HTTP 200. For both `grok-4.6-vertex` and `grok-4.6-direct`, `model_info.supports_prompt_caching` is `true`, and the Vertex row still shows `cache_read_input_token_cost` of `5e-07`.
4. I send `POST http://localhost:4000/v1/chat/completions` for `grok-4.6-vertex` with a long stable system prefix, a first user turn, and header `x-grok-conv-id: conv_repro_1`. I get HTTP 200 and `usage.prompt_tokens_details.cached_tokens` of `0`.
5. I send the same URL again with the same `x-grok-conv-id`, appending the assistant reply and a follow-up user turn. I get HTTP 200 and `usage.prompt_tokens_details.cached_tokens` greater than `0`.
6. I send `POST http://localhost:4000/v1/responses` for `grok-4.6-vertex` with the same prefix and `"prompt_cache_key": "conv_repro_1"`. I get HTTP 200 and `usage.input_tokens_details.cached_tokens` of `0`.
7. I send the same URL again with the same `prompt_cache_key` and the follow-up turn. I get HTTP 200 and `usage.input_tokens_details.cached_tokens` greater than `0`.

title: [Bug]: Databricks service_tier is dropped in request translation, streaming, and pricing

judge.reasoning: Patch A only adds `service_tier` to the Databricks supported-params list, fixes the Responses-to-Chat request read, and preserves the tier in `transform_response`. It does nothing for streaming (the tier arriving only on the terminal usage-only chunk is still lost in `CustomStreamWrapper`), nor for Chat-to-Responses or Chat-to-Messages response conversion. The independent tests confirm this: A fails the terminal-usage-chunk aggregation test, the Responses and Messages returned-tier preservation tests, and the streamed-default-overrides-requested-priority pricing test, which the issue explicitly calls out as the reason the defects must be fixed together. Patch B covers the same request-side fixes (with a safe `or kwargs.get` fallback) and additionally stamps the served tier from usage-only chunks in the stream wrapper, propagates it into the Responses API response, adds a `served_service_tier` helper that never manufactures a tier, threads it through the Anthropic Messages adapter for both non-streaming responses and the streaming `message_delta` usage (sync and async), and extends the TypedDicts accordingly. B passes all 13 independent tests. B's own test file is far more thorough, covering pricing precedence, legacy model resolution, drop_params mapping, no-manufactured-tier cases, stream aggregation via the real Databricks iterator and `CustomStreamWrapper`, and the Messages bridge end-to-end to cost. A's tests only cover the three narrow paths it fixed. B's extra scope is directly demanded by the issue, not churn, and is implemented consistently with surrounding conventions (Final annotations, setattr with noqa for pydantic extras).

issue_md:
## Summary

In LiteLLM 1.100.0, Databricks `service_tier="priority"` can be dropped during request translation and parameter filtering. Databricks cost calculation also ignores the resolved tier, so configured priority input/output/cache-read rates are not used. Returned tiers are lost in response conversion and streaming aggregation.

These defects need to be handled together: fixing pricing alone can apply requested priority rates even when Databricks reports `service_tier="default"` after fallback.

## Reproduction and environment

Reproduced with a clean installation of `litellm[proxy]==1.100.0` on Python 3.11 in an isolated virtual environment. The portable pytest file will be attached in a follow-up comment. It uses synthetic model prices and response objects; no API credentials, provider calls, proxy, or downstream repository files are required.

Save the attached file as `test_databricks_service_tier_upstream.py`, outside any existing checkout, and run:

```bash
python3 -m venv /tmp/databricks-tier-repro
/tmp/databricks-tier-repro/bin/pip install 'litellm[proxy]==1.100.0' pytest
LITELLM_LOCAL_MODEL_COST_MAP=True /tmp/databricks-tier-repro/bin/python -m pytest -q test_databricks_service_tier_upstream.py
```

Observed results: **6 failed, 7 passed**.

| Case | Expected | Actual on 1.100.0 |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Priority pricing from explicit argument, request params, or response | $0.000568 | $0.000284 in all three cases |
| Responses-to-Chat request translation | `service_tier="priority"` preserved | Field absent (`KeyError`) |
| Databricks parameter mapping with `drop_params=True` | `service_tier="priority"` preserved | Field absent (`KeyError`) |
| Stream with tier on terminal usage-only chunk | Aggregated response has `service_tier="default"` | `None` |

The synthetic pricing case has 100 input tokens (20 cached) and 50 output tokens. Standard rates are $1/$4 per million input/output tokens and $0.20 per million cached input tokens; priority rates are twice those values.

Default pricing, legacy Databricks model resolution, and returned-default fallback controls pass on stock 1.100.0. The fallback controls pass because stock Databricks pricing always uses standard rates; they must continue to pass after priority pricing is enabled. All 13 tests pass with a local fix.

## Root cause

Source locations refer to LiteLLM 1.100.0:

- `litellm/llms/databricks/chat/transformation.py`, `DatabricksConfig.get_supported_openai_params` (~line 259): `service_tier` is absent from the supported parameter list.
- `litellm/responses/litellm_completion_transformation/transformation.py`, `transform_responses_api_request_to_chat_completion_request` (~line 340): reads `kwargs.get("service_tier")`, but the tier is in `responses_api_request`. Adding only the Databricks allowlist entry does not repair this earlier loss.
- `litellm/cost_calculator.py` (~line 623) and `litellm/llms/databricks/cost_calculator.py` (~line 34): the Databricks dispatch/helper do not pass `service_tier` through to `generic_cost_per_token`.
- `litellm/litellm_core_utils/streaming_chunk_builder_utils.py`: stream aggregation does not carry the returned tier, including when it arrives only on the final usage chunk. Databricks response parsing, stream-wrapper reconstruction, and Chat/Responses/Messages conversion also need to preserve it for end-to-end accounting.
- `completion_cost` currently gives a requested tier precedence over a returned tier. For Databricks, a concrete returned `default` tier should override requested priority.

Additional Router/HTTP-interception tests exposed a related Messages-stream accounting issue: `litellm/llms/anthropic/experimental_pass_through/adapters/streaming_iterator.py` calls `stream_chunk_builder` without its existing request logging object. Standalone cost calculation can then miss Router pricing and cache a zero cost. Passing the logging object preserves the configured pricing context. This path is covered by the broader local regression suite, not the 13-test portable file.

## Expected behavior

- Forward supported Databricks `default`/`priority` tiers through Chat, Responses, and Messages bridges, including streaming.
- Preserve provider-returned tiers through response parsing, adapters, stream reconstruction/aggregation, and accounting.
- Apply configured tier-specific input, output, and cache-read prices.
- Use a concrete returned Databricks tier over the requested tier; retain standard pricing and legacy model-name resolution.
- If the provider omits a returned tier, do not manufacture one. Requested-tier pricing is an estimate, not evidence of the tier delivered or invoiced.

Databricks documents priority fallback and model/region availability here: https://docs.databricks.com/aws/en/machine-learning/foundation-model-apis/priority-mode

I searched open and closed issues for Databricks priority/service-tier symptoms and the affected function names and found no matching report. PR #35674 concerns cache pricing and does not address these tier-propagation gaps.

title: [Bug]: Vertex Grok (`vertex_ai/xai/grok-*`) is rejected on `/v1beta/models/{model}:generateContent` while `/v1/chat/completions` on the same deployment works

judge.reasoning:
Both patches fix the root cause identically in spirit: `ProviderConfigManager.get_provider_google_genai_generate_content_config` now defers to `get_vertex_ai_model_route()` so `xai/grok-*` (and gemma/, agent_engine/, Model Garden, partner models) return None and fall through to the litellm.completion() adapter, exactly as the issue's 'narrow fix' suggests. All five independent tests pass on both, so correctness on the reported scenarios is equal.

Patch A stays tight: the utils.py selection change, a small type tightening in common_utils, a low-risk guard so countTokens on Model Garden models falls back to local counting (tested), and focused unit tests that drive the real `agenerate_content`/`agenerate_content_stream` path through a mocked Model Garden chat-completions endpoint, asserting the Gemini publisher URL is not hit and the candidates text is '144'. Those tests would fail on base and pass after, and they map directly to steps 5 and 6 of the issue.

Patch B lands the same core fix (plus base_model plumbing from GenerateContentHelper, a mild parity improvement) but buries it under a large unrelated rewrite: cost_calculator prefix-lookup logic in the billing path, a full restructuring of the google_genai adapter handler (exception type changes, stream_options injection, logging-complete markers), stream-wrapper usage-chunk holding/reordering, a rewrite of the databricks ModelResponseIterator iteration semantics used by several providers, a proxy stream_usage_tracking change, and type changes. Each of these touches hot paths well beyond the issue's ask and carries regression risk (billing, streaming for all databricks-style providers, error surfaces). The accompanying tests are mostly heavy integration tests needing a database, wire servers, owned proxy processes with worker-kill orchestration and psutil, which makes the fix hard to review and verify. Under the stated criteria, this extra work earns no credit and counts against B where it adds risk and obscures the fix, which it clearly does here.

On craft, A's enum-tuple check is explicit and readable; B's `uses_vertex_gemini_api` helper is also clean, but that advantage is outweighed by the scope problem. A is the better fix.

issue_md:
### Check for existing issues

- [x] I have searched the existing issues and checked that my issue is not a duplicate.

### What happened?

A proxy with a single Vertex Model Garden Grok deployment (`vertex_ai/xai/grok-4.6`) serves that model correctly on `/v1/chat/completions`, but the same `model_name` on the unified Gemini-style endpoint `POST /v1beta/models/grok-4.6:generateContent` fails.

On the same proxy and the same endpoint:

- `gemini-*` deployments succeed.
- Vertex Claude deployments succeed (they are translated to their own chat protocol).
- `vertex_ai/xai/grok-*` deployments fail.

**Expected:** `/v1beta/models/{model}:generateContent` should serve a Vertex `xai/grok-*` deployment the same way it already serves other non-Gemini Vertex publisher models (Claude, Mistral, gpt-oss, Qwen, MiniMax, Moonshot, Z.ai, Gemma MaaS) — by translating the request to that model's chat-completions protocol and returning a normal `candidates[...]` response — instead of treating Grok as a native Gemini model.

**Suspected cause (for maintainers):** two different checks decide how a Vertex model is served, and they disagree about the `xai/` publisher.

- `litellm/llms/vertex_ai/common_utils.py::get_vertex_ai_model_route()` has an explicit `model.startswith("xai/")` branch returning `MODEL_GARDEN`, so chat completions work.
- `litellm/utils.py::ProviderConfigManager.get_provider_google_genai_generate_content_config()` falls back to the `litellm.completion()` adapter only when `VertexAIPartnerModels.is_vertex_partner_model()` is true, and `PartnerModelPrefixes` has no `xai/` entry, so Grok is handed to `VertexAIGoogleGenAIConfig` (native Gemini) instead.

Note that simply adding `xai/` to `PartnerModelPrefixes` would regress chat completions: `is_vertex_partner_model()` is evaluated before the `xai/` Model Garden branch, and the partner handler raises `Unknown partner model` for `xai/`. The narrow fix is to make the `generateContent` handler selection use the same Model Garden determination that chat routing already uses.

### User Flow

**Before a (hypothetical) fix** — the flow breaks the first time the user sends a Grok request to the Gemini-style URL, even though every other model at that same URL works and Grok itself works at the OpenAI-style URL.

1. The user lists the gateway catalog with `GET http://localhost:4000/v1/models` and sees both `gemini-2.5-flash` and `grok-4.6` offered.
2. The user sends `POST http://localhost:4000/v1/chat/completions` with `{"model": "grok-4.6", "messages": [{"role": "user", "content": "What is 12*12? Reply with only the number."}]}` and gets `200` with `choices[0].message.content` = `144`.
3. The user points their Google GenAI SDK app at the gateway and sends `POST http://localhost:4000/v1beta/models/gemini-2.5-flash:generateContent` with `{"contents": [...]}` and gets `200` with `candidates[0].content.parts[0].text` = `144`.
4. The user sends the identical body to `POST http://localhost:4000/v1beta/models/claude-opus-4-5:generateContent` for their Vertex Claude deployment and gets `200` with the same `candidates[...]` shape, confirming the endpoint is not Gemini-only.
5. The user sends the identical body to `POST http://localhost:4000/v1beta/models/grok-4.6:generateContent` and instead of `200` gets an error naming the Gemini publisher path for a model that is not a Gemini publisher model.
6. The user retries streaming at `POST http://localhost:4000/v1beta/models/grok-4.6:streamGenerateContent` and gets the same failure, with no chunks.

+def _grok_chat_completion_sse(text_pieces: list[str]) -> bytes:
+    deltas: Final = [{"role": "assistant", "content": text_pieces[0]}] + [{"content": t} for t in text_pieces[1:]]
+    chunks: Final = [
+        {
+            "id": "chatcmpl-grok",
+            "object": "chat.completion.chunk",
+            "created": 1,
+            "model": "xai/grok-4.6",
+            "choices": [{"index": 0, "delta": delta}],
+        }
+        for delta in deltas
+    ] + [
+        {
+            "id": "chatcmpl-grok",
+            "object": "chat.completion.chunk",
+            "created": 1,
+            "model": "xai/grok-4.6",
+            "choices": [{"index": 0, "delta": {}, "finish_reason": "stop"}],
+        }
+    ]
+    return ("".join(f"data: {json.dumps(c)}\n\n" for c in chunks) + "data: [DONE]\n\n").encode()
+

+def _streamed_candidate_text(raw_stream: bytes) -> str:
+    text = ""
+    for line in raw_stream.decode().splitlines():
+        if not line.startswith("data: "):
+            continue
+        event = json.loads(line[len("data: ") :])
+        for candidate in event.get("candidates", []):
+            for part in candidate.get("content", {}).get("parts", []):
+                text += part.get("text", "")
+    return text

+import json
+import uuid
+from collections.abc import Callable, Mapping, Sequence
+from dataclasses import dataclass
+from hashlib import sha256
+from typing import Final
+
+import httpx
+import pytest
+from integration._support.client import Gateway, Scenario, eventually, held, object_value
+from integration._support.database import read_rows
+from integration._support.vertex import service_account_json
+from integration._support.wire import Reply, Request, Wire, wire_server
+from pydantic import JsonValue, TypeAdapter
+
+_JSON_OBJECT: Final = TypeAdapter(dict[str, JsonValue])
+_PROJECT: Final = "scripted-project"
+_REPLY_TEXT: Final = "scripted vertex reply"
+_PROMPT_TOKENS: Final = 11
+_COMPLETION_TOKENS: Final = 7
+_USAGE: Final = {
+    "promptTokenCount": _PROMPT_TOKENS,
+    "candidatesTokenCount": _COMPLETION_TOKENS,
+    "totalTokenCount": _PROMPT_TOKENS + _COMPLETION_TOKENS,
+}
+_NATIVE_COUNT: Final = 31
+_SPEND_SELECT: Final = (
+    "SELECT request_id, call_type, model_group, status, cache_hit, prompt_tokens, completion_tokens, spend"
+    ' FROM "LiteLLM_SpendLogs" WHERE api_key=%s ORDER BY "startTime"'
+)
+
+
+@dataclass(frozen=True, slots=True)
+class Route:
+    model: str
+    location: str
+    adapter: bool
+    endpoint_path: str = ""
+    overrides: Mapping[str, JsonValue] | None = None
+
+
+_ROUTES: Final = {
+    "model_garden_publisher": Route("xai/grok-4.20-non-reasoning", "global", adapter=True),
+    "model_garden_endpoint": Route("openai/1234567890123456789", "us-central1", adapter=True),
+    "gemma": Route(
+        "gemma/gemma-2-2b-it",
+        "us-central1",
+        adapter=True,
+        endpoint_path=f"/v1/projects/{_PROJECT}/locations/us-central1/endpoints/4242:predict",
+    ),
+    "gemini": Route("gemini-2.5-flash", "us-central1", adapter=False),
+    "legacy_non_gemini": Route("chat-bison", "us-central1", adapter=False),
+    "tuned_gemini_endpoint": Route(
+        "9876543210", "us-central1", adapter=False, overrides={"base_model": "vertex_ai/gemini-2.5-flash"}
+    ),
+}
+_ADAPTER_ROUTES: Final = tuple(name for name, route in _ROUTES.items() if route.adapter)
+
+
+def _openai_reply(model: str) -> dict[str, JsonValue]:
+    return {
+        "id": f"chatcmpl-{uuid.uuid4().hex}",
+        "object": "chat.completion",
+        "created": 1700000000,
+        "model": model,
+        "choices": [{"index": 0, "message": {"role": "assistant", "content": _REPLY_TEXT}, "finish_reason": "stop"}],
+        "usage": {
+            "prompt_tokens": _PROMPT_TOKENS,
+            "completion_tokens": _COMPLETION_TOKENS,
+            "total_tokens": _PROMPT_TOKENS + _COMPLETION_TOKENS,
+        },
+    }
+
+
+def _openai_frames(model: str, include_usage: bool) -> tuple[bytes, ...]:
+    base: Final = {
+        "id": f"chatcmpl-{uuid.uuid4().hex}",
+        "object": "chat.completion.chunk",
+        "created": 1700000000,
+        "model": model,
+    }
+
+    def frame(chunk: Mapping[str, JsonValue]) -> bytes:
+        return f"data: {json.dumps({**base, **chunk})}\n\n".encode()
+
+    usage: Final = (frame({"choices": [], "usage": _openai_reply(model)["usage"]}),) if include_usage else ()
+    return (
+        frame(
+            {"choices": [{"index": 0, "delta": {"role": "assistant", "content": _REPLY_TEXT}, "finish_reason": None}]}
+        ),
+        frame({"choices": [{"index": 0, "delta": {}, "finish_reason": "stop"}]}),
+        *usage,
+        b"data: [DONE]\n\n",
+    )
+
+
+def _asks_for_usage(body: Mapping[str, JsonValue]) -> bool:
+    options: Final = body.get("stream_options")
+    return isinstance(options, dict) and options.get("include_usage") is True
+
+
+def _native_reply() -> dict[str, JsonValue]:
+    return {
+        "candidates": [
+            {"content": {"parts": [{"text": _REPLY_TEXT}], "role": "model"}, "finishReason": "STOP", "index": 0}
+        ],
+        "usageMetadata": _USAGE,
+    }
+
+
+def _native_frames() -> tuple[bytes, ...]:
+    return (
+        b'data: {"candidates":[{"content":{"parts":[{"text":"'
+        + _REPLY_TEXT.encode()
+        + b'"}],"role":"model"},"index":0}]}\n\n',
+        b'data: {"candidates":[{"content":{"parts":[],"role":"model"},"finishReason":"STOP","index":0}],"usageMetadata":'
+        + json.dumps(_USAGE).encode()
+        + b"}\n\n",
+    )
+
+
+def _publisher_not_found(request: Request) -> Reply:
+    return Reply(
+        status=404,
+        body=json.dumps(
+            {
+                "error": {
+                    "code": 404,
+                    "message": f"Publisher Model {request.target} was not found",
+                    "status": "NOT_FOUND",
+                }
+            }
+        ).encode(),
+    )
+
+
+def _google_native_target(target: str) -> bool:
+    return any(
+        name in target for name in ("/models/gemini-2.5-flash:", "/models/chat-bison:", "/endpoints/9876543210:")
+    )
+
+
+def _vertex_peer(status: int = 200, error: str = "scripted vertex rejection") -> Callable[[Request], Reply]:
+    def respond(request: Request) -> Reply:
+        if status != 200:
+            return Reply(status=status, body=json.dumps({"error": {"message": error, "code": status}}).encode())
+        if request.target.endswith("/chat/completions"):
+            body: Final = _JSON_OBJECT.validate_json(request.body)
+            model: Final = str(body.get("model", ""))
+            if body.get("stream") is True:
+                return Reply(content_type="text/event-stream", chunks=_openai_frames(model, _asks_for_usage(body)))
+            return Reply(body=json.dumps(_openai_reply(model)).encode())
+        if request.target.endswith(":predict"):
+            return Reply(body=json.dumps({"predictions": _openai_reply("gemma-2-2b-it")}).encode())
+        if not _google_native_target(request.target):
+            return _publisher_not_found(request)
+        if ":streamGenerateContent" in request.target:
+            return Reply(content_type="text/event-stream", chunks=_native_frames())
+        if request.target.endswith(":countTokens"):
+            return Reply(body=json.dumps({"totalTokens": _NATIVE_COUNT}).encode())
+        return Reply(body=json.dumps(_native_reply()).encode())
+
+    return respond
+
+
+def _deployment(gateway: Gateway, scenario: Scenario, wire: Wire, route: Route, **extra: JsonValue) -> str:
+    return scenario.model(
+        model=f"vertex_ai/{route.model}",
+        api_base=f"{wire.url}{route.endpoint_path}",
+        api_key=None,
+        vertex_project=_PROJECT,
+        vertex_location=route.location,
+        vertex_credentials=service_account_json(_PROJECT, gateway.upstream_url.rstrip("/")),
+        **dict(route.overrides or {}),
+        **extra,
+    )
+
+
+def _contents(marker: str) -> list[JsonValue]:
+    return [{"role": "user", "parts": [{"text": f"route probe {marker}"}]}]
+
+
+def _generate(gateway: Gateway, model: str, key: str, body: Mapping[str, JsonValue]) -> httpx.Response:
+    return gateway.request("POST", f"/v1beta/models/{model}:generateContent", body, key=key)
+
+
+def _stream(gateway: Gateway, model: str, key: str, body: Mapping[str, JsonValue]) -> httpx.Response:
+    return gateway.client.post(
+        f"/v1beta/models/{model}:streamGenerateContent?alt=sse",
+        json=dict(body),
+        headers={"Authorization": f"Bearer {key}"},
+    )
+
+
+def _frames(response: httpx.Response) -> list[dict[str, JsonValue]]:
+    parts: Final = [part for part in response.text.split("\n\n") if part.strip()]
+    assert all(part.startswith("data: ") for part in parts), response.text
+    return [_JSON_OBJECT.validate_json(part.removeprefix("data: ")) for part in parts]
+
+
+def _finish_reasons(frames: Sequence[Mapping[str, JsonValue]]) -> list[JsonValue]:
+    return [
+        object_value(candidate).get("finishReason")
+        for frame in frames
+        for candidate in (frame.get("candidates") or [])  # comprehension-ok: two-level frame walk
+        if isinstance(candidate, dict) and candidate.get("finishReason")
+    ]
+
+
+def _text(frames: Sequence[Mapping[str, JsonValue]]) -> str:
+    return "".join(
+        str(object_value(part).get("text", ""))
+        for frame in frames
+        for candidate in (frame.get("candidates") or [])  # comprehension-ok: three-level frame walk
+        for part in object_value(object_value(candidate).get("content") or {}).get("parts") or []
+    )
+
+
+def _spend_rows(key: str, count: int) -> list[dict[str, JsonValue]]:
+    digest: Final = sha256(key.encode()).hexdigest()
+    eventually(lambda: read_rows(_SPEND_SELECT, (digest,)), lambda values: len(values) >= count, seconds=70)
+    return held(lambda: read_rows(_SPEND_SELECT, (digest,)), lambda values: len(values) == count, holding=3)
+
+
+def _route_targets(wire: Wire) -> list[tuple[str, str]]:
+    return [(request.method, request.target) for request in wire.drain()]
+
+
+def _expected_adapter_target(route: Route) -> str:
+    return route.endpoint_path if route.endpoint_path else "/chat/completions"
+
+
+def _cost_map_prices(gateway: Gateway, model: str) -> tuple[float, float]:
+    entries: Final = gateway.get("/model/info")["data"]
+    assert isinstance(entries, list)
+    info: Final = next(
+        object_value(object_value(entry)["model_info"])
+        for entry in entries
+        if object_value(entry)["model_name"] == model
+    )
+    prompt: Final = info.get("input_cost_per_token")
+    completion: Final = info.get("output_cost_per_token")
+    assert isinstance(prompt, float) and isinstance(completion, float) and prompt > 0 and completion > 0, info
+    return prompt, completion
+

+@pytest.mark.parametrize("route_name", tuple(_ROUTES))
+def test_generate_content_reaches_the_route_handler_chat_uses(gateway: Gateway, route_name: str) -> None:
+    route: Final = _ROUTES[route_name]
+    with wire_server(_vertex_peer()) as wire, gateway.scenario() as scenario:
+        model: Final = _deployment(gateway, scenario, wire, route)
+        key: Final = scenario.key(models=[model])
+        response: Final = _generate(gateway, model, key, {"contents": _contents(uuid.uuid4().hex)})
+        assert response.status_code == 200, response.text
+        body: Final = _JSON_OBJECT.validate_json(response.content)
+        assert _text([body]) == _REPLY_TEXT, response.text
+        assert _finish_reasons([body]) == ["STOP"], response.text
+        assert body["usageMetadata"] == _USAGE, response.text
+        targets: Final = _route_targets(wire)
+        assert len(targets) == 1, targets
+        if route.adapter:
+            assert targets == [("POST", _expected_adapter_target(route))], targets
+        else:
+            assert targets[0][1].endswith(":generateContent"), targets
+        rows: Final = _spend_rows(key, 1)
+        assert rows[0]["model_group"] == model, rows
+        assert (rows[0]["prompt_tokens"], rows[0]["completion_tokens"]) == (_PROMPT_TOKENS, _COMPLETION_TOKENS), rows
+

+@pytest.mark.parametrize("route_name", tuple(_ROUTES))
+def test_stream_generate_content_ends_with_one_stop_carrying_upstream_usage(gateway: Gateway, route_name: str) -> None:
+    route: Final = _ROUTES[route_name]
+    with wire_server(_vertex_peer()) as wire, gateway.scenario() as scenario:
+        model: Final = _deployment(gateway, scenario, wire, route)
+        key: Final = scenario.key(models=[model])
+        response: Final = _stream(gateway, model, key, {"contents": _contents(uuid.uuid4().hex)})
+        assert response.status_code == 200, response.text
+        frames: Final = _frames(response)
+        assert _text(frames) == _REPLY_TEXT, response.text
+        assert _finish_reasons(frames) == ["STOP"], response.text
+        assert _finish_reasons(frames[-1:]) == ["STOP"], response.text
+        assert frames[-1]["usageMetadata"] == _USAGE, response.text
+        received: Final = wire.drain()
+        assert len(received) == 1, [request.target for request in received]
+        if route.adapter and not route.endpoint_path:
+            assert received[0].target == "/chat/completions", received[0].target
+            assert _JSON_OBJECT.validate_json(received[0].body)["stream_options"] == {"include_usage": True}
+        if not route.adapter:
+            assert ":streamGenerateContent" in received[0].target, received[0].target
+            assert "stream_options" not in _JSON_OBJECT.validate_json(received[0].body), received[0].body
+        rows: Final = _spend_rows(key, 1)
+        assert rows[0]["model_group"] == model, rows
+        assert (rows[0]["prompt_tokens"], rows[0]["completion_tokens"]) == (_PROMPT_TOKENS, _COMPLETION_TOKENS), rows

+def test_adapter_route_cache_hit_skips_the_upstream_and_keeps_attribution(
+    gateway: Gateway, route_name: str, streamed: bool
+) -> None:
+    route: Final = _ROUTES[route_name]

+        first: Final = call(gateway, model, key, body)

+        replayed: Final = _replayed_frames(second, streamed)

+        rows: Final = _spend_rows(key, 2)

+        assert [row["model_group"] for row in rows] == [model, model], rows

+def test_adapter_route_failure_leaves_other_keys_serving(gateway: Gateway) -> None:

+    with (

+        gateway.scenario() as scenario,
+    ):

+        working: Final = _deployment(gateway, scenario, serving, route)

+        served: Final = _generate(gateway, working, working_key, {"contents": _contents("b")})

+_GEMINI_USAGE: Final = {
+    "promptTokenCount": _PROMPT_TOKENS,

+_REJECTION: Final = "scripted key rejected"

+def _frame(chunk: Mapping[str, JsonValue]) -> bytes:
+    body: Final = {
+        "id": "chatcmpl-sdk",
+        "object": "chat.completion.chunk",
+        "created": 1700000000,
+        "model": "m",
+        **chunk,
+    }
+    return f"data: {json.dumps(body)}\n\n".encode()
+
+
+def _frames(include_usage: bool) -> tuple[bytes, ...]:
+    usage: Final = (_frame({"choices": [], "usage": _USAGE}),) if include_usage else ()
+    return (
+        _frame({"choices": [{"index": 0, "delta": {"role": "assistant", "content": _REPLY_TEXT}}]}),
+        b"\n\n",
+        _frame({"choices": [{"index": 0, "delta": {}, "finish_reason": "stop"}]}),

+def _asks_for_usage(body: Mapping[str, JsonValue]) -> bool:

+    return isinstance(options, dict) and options.get("include_usage") is True

+
+def _respond(status: int) -> Callable[[Request], Reply]:
+    def respond(request: Request) -> Reply:
+        if request.target.endswith("/_oauth/token"):
+            return Reply(body=_TOKEN)
+        if status != 200:
+            return Reply(status=status, body=json.dumps({"error": {"message": _REJECTION, "code": status}}).encode())
+        body: Final = _JSON_OBJECT.validate_json(request.body)
+        return Reply(
+            content_type="text/event-stream", chunks=_frames(_asks_for_usage(body) or "/ml/v1/" in request.target)
+        )
+
+    return respond
+
+
+@pytest.fixture
+def wire() -> Iterator[Wire]:
+    with wire_server(_respond(200)) as served:

+
+class _FailureCounter(CustomLogger):
+    def __init__(self) -> None:
+        super().__init__()
+        self._lock: Final = threading.Lock()
+        self._failures: Final[list[str]] = []
+
+    def log_failure_event(
+        self, kwargs: dict[str, object], response_obj: object, start_time: object, end_time: object
+    ) -> None:
+        with self._lock:
+            self._failures.append("sync")
+
+    async def async_log_failure_event(
+        self, kwargs: dict[str, object], response_obj: object, start_time: object, end_time: object
+    ) -> None:
+        with self._lock:
+            self._failures.append("async")
+
+    def failures(self) -> tuple[str, ...]:
+        with self._lock:
+            return tuple(self._failures)
+
+
+def _logged_once(counter: _FailureCounter, kind: str) -> tuple[str, ...]:

+        owned: Final = stack.enter_context(owned_proxy_process(gateway, tmp_path, {}, config=config, workers=2))

+        for caller in _CALLER_OPTIONS:

+                owned.gateway.client, scenario.key(models=[_ADAPTER_MODEL]), wire, setting, caller

+    return read_rows(_BURST_SELECT, (",".join(digests),))

+    eventually(lambda: _burst_rows(digests), lambda rows: len(rows) >= expected, seconds=120)
+    return held(lambda: _burst_rows(digests), lambda rows: len(rows) == expected, holding=5)

+def _stream_or_dropped(client: httpx.Client, key: str) -> httpx.Response | None:
+    try:
+        return _stream(client, _ADAPTER_MODEL, key, _stream_body(uuid.uuid4().hex, None))
+    except httpx.TransportError:
+        return None

+def _local_port(client: httpx.Client) -> int:
+    with client.stream("GET", "/health/liveliness") as response:

+    return frozenset(
+        connection.raddr.port
+        for connection in psutil.Process(pid).net_connections(kind="tcp")
+        if connection.raddr and connection.laddr.port == proxy_port
+    )

+    gate: Final = threading.Event()
+    with ExitStack() as stack:
+        wire: Final = stack.enter_context(wire_server(_peer(gate)))
+        stack.callback(gate.set)
+        config: Final = _owned_config(tmp_path / "worker-kill.yaml", gateway, wire, {})
+        owned: Final = stack.enter_context(owned_proxy_process(gateway, tmp_path, {}, config=config, workers=2))
+        workers: Final = eventually(
+            lambda: tuple(int(pid) for pid in _STARTED_WORKER.findall(owned.log.read_text())),
+            lambda pids: len(pids) == 2,
+            seconds=30,
+        )
+        scenario: Final = stack.enter_context(owned.gateway.scenario())
+        proxy_url: Final = owned.gateway.client.base_url
+        clients: Final = tuple(
+            stack.enter_context(httpx.Client(base_url=str(proxy_url), timeout=60, trust_env=False)) for _ in range(12)
+        )
+        keys: Final = tuple(scenario.key(models=[_ADAPTER_MODEL]) for _ in clients)
+        ports: Final = tuple(_local_port(client) for client in clients)
+        pool: Final = stack.enter_context(ThreadPoolExecutor(max_workers=len(clients)))
+        futures: Final = tuple(
+            pool.submit(_stream_or_dropped, client, key) for client, key in zip(clients, keys, strict=True)
+        )
+        eventually(wire.received.qsize, lambda size: size >= len(clients), seconds=60)
+        shares: Final = {pid: _accepted_client_ports(pid, proxy_url.port or 0) & frozenset(ports) for pid in workers}
+        assert sum(map(len, shares.values())) == len(clients), shares
+        victim: Final = min((pid for pid in workers if shares[pid]), key=lambda pid: len(shares[pid]))
+        with owned.replacing_worker(victim) as kill:
+            kill()
+            gate.set()
+            results: Final = tuple(future.result(timeout=60) for future in futures)
+        survivors: Final = tuple(
+            (key, result) for port, key, result in zip(ports, keys, results, strict=True) if port not in shares[victim]
+        )
+        assert survivors, shares
+        for _, result in survivors:
+            assert result is not None
+            _assert_one_stop_with(result, _GEMINI_USAGE)
+        second_keys: Final = tuple(scenario.key(models=[_ADAPTER_MODEL]) for _ in range(6))
+        second: Final = tuple(_stream_or_dropped(owned.gateway.client, key) for key in second_keys)
+        for result in second:
+            assert result is not None
+            _assert_one_stop_with(result, _GEMINI_USAGE)
+        billed: Final = tuple(key for key, _ in survivors) + second_keys
+        digests: Final = tuple(sha256(key.encode()).hexdigest() for key in billed)
+        rows: Final = _rows_by_key(digests, len(billed))
+        assert sorted(str(row["api_key"]) for row in rows) == sorted(digests)
+        assert {(row["prompt_tokens"], row["completion_tokens"]) for row in rows} == {
+            (_PROMPT_TOKENS, _COMPLETION_TOKENS)
+        }, rows
+        assert owned.process.poll() is None

+        "created": 1700000000,

+_FINISH: Final = _chunk([{"index": 0, "delta": {}, "finish_reason": "stop"}])
+_USAGE_ONLY: Final = _chunk([], usage=_DETAILED_USAGE)
+_DONE: Final = b"data: [DONE]\n\n"

+            "id": f"chatcmpl-{uuid.uuid4().hex}",
+            "object": "chat.completion",
+            "created": 1700000000,
+            "model": "scripted",
+            "choices": [

+            "usage": _USAGE,

+        if _JSON_OBJECT.validate_json(request.body).get("stream") is True:
+            return Reply(content_type="text/event-stream", chunks=frames)
+        return Reply(body=_reply_json())

+    return respond

title: [Feature]: Expose OpenTelemetry trace IDs on LiteLLM Proxy responses

judge.reasoning: The issue asks for a specific header, `x-litellm-trace-id`, carrying the bare 32-character lowercase W3C trace ID. Patch A adds exactly that: a `TraceIdHeaderMiddleware` nested inside the OTel server-span middleware that anchors the recording server span on `request.state`, writes the header on `http.response.start` (so JSON and streaming initial headers both get it), stamps `litellm.call_id` onto the root span from the response's `x-litellm-call-id`, and handles the two out-of-middleware paths (the `Exception` handler via `with_trace_id_header`, and the legacy-logger span that `_close_dangling_otel_server_span` ends early) plus the OpenTelemetry logger's own early-end paths. It covers both the V2 FastAPI-instrumented span and the legacy `user_api_key_auth`-created span, omits the header when OTel is absent, unsampled, or the route is excluded, and preserves incoming `traceparent`. Its unit tests exercise success, streaming, 400/401/403/429/502 ProxyExceptions, 422 validation, unhandled 500, traceparent propagation, omission cases, legacy mode, and middleware ordering. Patch B instead emits a `traceresponse` header in `00-<trace>-<span>-<flags>` format and never adds `x-litellm-trace-id` at all, so it does not deliver the requested contract; the independent tests confirm every trace-id-header test fails on B while passing on A (only the `litellm.call_id` span-attribute tests pass on B). B is also V2-only (the issue's repro uses V2, but the feature statement is unconditional on a recording server span), and it adds substantial unrelated scope: upstream `traceresponse` relaying and span linking for passthroughs, CORS expose-header changes, a propagator override, and a ~700-line integration test rig. That extra work does not offset the missing deliverable and adds risk. A resolves the issue; B does not.

## Check for existing issues

- [x] I have searched the existing issues and checked that my issue is not a duplicate

## The Feature

Add `x-litellm-trace-id` to LiteLLM Proxy HTTP responses whenever the request has a recording OpenTelemetry server span. Its value should be the root trace ID as a 32-character lowercase W3C trace ID

The response already includes `x-litellm-call-id`, but a gateway user who receives that ID cannot reliably open the exact trace that handled the request. The proposed response header would make a client response, the request trace, and the existing call ID directly navigable across tracing and logging backends

For any response that has both values, the root server span should also carry the same `litellm.call_id` as `x-litellm-call-id`. This establishes an explicit relationship between the response, root span, and downstream LLM spans

Expected behavior:

1. Return the header on successful JSON responses and the initial headers of streaming responses
2. Return the header on validation, authentication, authorization, rate-limit, provider, and unhandled-error responses
3. Preserve incoming `traceparent` propagation and return the resulting request trace ID
4. Omit the header when OpenTelemetry is disabled or no recording request span exists
5. Keep `x-litellm-call-id` behavior unchanged

This is a LiteLLM Proxy / AI Gateway feature only. It does not change the Python SDK or WebSocket behavior

Related: #31864 covers request identity in JSON logs. This request covers the gateway HTTP response and its OpenTelemetry root span

## User Flow

Before this feature (today): a gateway developer investigating a failed model request reaches the response's call ID but cannot navigate directly to the trace that handled it

1. They send `POST https://gateway.example.com/v1/chat/completions` with their model and messages
2. The gateway returns `400 Bad Request` or a provider error with `x-litellm-call-id: 7ac48d62-40a1-44e6-8b50-19da641835a5`
3. They search the observability backend for that call ID and manually inspect matching LLM spans, logs, or request time ranges to identify the parent request trace
4. Their workaround is to correlate timestamps and child-span fields, which is slow and ambiguous when several retries or requests are in flight

After this feature (ideal user flow): the same developer can open the exact request trace from the gateway response

1. They send the same `POST https://gateway.example.com/v1/chat/completions` with the same model and messages
2. The gateway returns the same status and `x-litellm-call-id`, plus `x-litellm-trace-id: af353cab815b907430a117c9b97b4d0e`
3. They paste `af353cab815b907430a117c9b97b4d0e` into their observability backend and open the one server trace for that gateway request
4. They use the call ID visible on that trace to correlate request logs and downstream model spans without matching timestamps by hand

## How far you got

Config / setup the proxy ran with:

```yaml
model_list: []
general_settings:
  master_key: sk-local-trace-repro
litellm_settings:
  telemetry: false
```

Version or commit: `5417abd58672` on the current `main` branch

Environment variables: `LITELLM_OTEL_V2=true`, `OTEL_EXPORTER=console`, and `OTEL_SERVICE_NAME=litellm-trace-header-repro`

Commands and their full output, up to the step that dead-ends:

```console
$ LITELLM_OTEL_V2=true OTEL_EXPORTER=console OTEL_SERVICE_NAME=litellm-trace-header-repro uv run litellm --config /private/tmp/litellm-trace-header-repro.yaml --host 127.0.0.1 --port 4000
INFO:     Application startup complete.
INFO:     Uvicorn running on http://127.0.0.1:4000 (Press CTRL+C to quit)

$ curl --max-time 15 -i -X POST http://127.0.0.1:4000/v1/chat/completions -H 'Authorization: Bearer sk-local-trace-repro' -H 'Content-Type: application/json' --data '{"model":"missing-model","messages":[{"role":"user","content":"hello"}]}'
HTTP/1.1 400 Bad Request
date: Sun, 20 Sep 2026 02:32:23 GMT
x-litellm-call-id: 7ac48d62-40a1-44e6-8b50-19da641835a5

x-litellm-key-spend: 0.0

{"error":{"message":"/chat/completions: Invalid model name passed in model=missing-model. Call `/v1/models` to view available models for your key.","type":"invalid_request_error","param":null,"code":"400","provider_specific_fields":{"error":"/chat/completions: Invalid model name passed in model=missing-model. Call `/v1/models` to view available models for your key."}}}
```

The console exporter emitted this server span for the same request:

```console
{
    "name": "POST /v1/chat/completions",
    "context": {
        "trace_id": "0xaf353cab815b907430a117c9b97b4d0e",
        "span_id": "0x20cb45e2212a998e"
    },
    "kind": "SpanKind.SERVER",
    "status": {
        "status_code": "ERROR"
    }
}
```

What stopped me there: the live proxy created a server trace with ID `af353cab815b907430a117c9b97b4d0e` and returned a different call ID, but the HTTP response did not expose the trace ID. A client receiving the error therefore cannot navigate straight to the trace

## Which part of LiteLLM is this about?

Logging: callbacks, Langfuse, Datadog, OTel, Prometheus, alerting

diff --git a/litellm/proxy/middleware/trace_id_header_middleware.py b/litellm/proxy/middleware/trace_id_header_middleware.py
new file mode 100644
index 0000000000..4c5eab53d9
--- /dev/null
+++ b/litellm/proxy/middleware/trace_id_header_middleware.py
@@ -0,0 +1,114 @@
+"""
+Exposes the request's OpenTelemetry trace ID as ``x-litellm-trace-id`` on every
+HTTP response, and stamps the response's ``x-litellm-call-id`` onto the request's
+root server span as ``litellm.call_id``.
+
+The root span is anchored on ``request.state`` the first time the proxy sees it:
+under OTel V2 that is the FastAPI instrumentation's SERVER span, active when this
+middleware runs because it is registered inside ``OpenTelemetryMiddleware``; under
+the legacy logger it is the span ``user_api_key_auth`` creates. Anchoring on
+``request.state`` rather than reading the active span at response time lets the
+unhandled-exception handler, which runs in ``ServerErrorMiddleware`` after the
+server span has ended, still answer with the trace ID.
+
+The header is omitted when OpenTelemetry is not installed, disabled, or the
+request has no recording span (excluded route, sampled out).
+"""
+
+from importlib.util import find_spec
+from typing import Final
+
+from starlette.datastructures import MutableHeaders, State
+from starlette.requests import Request
+from starlette.responses import Response
+from starlette.types import ASGIApp, Message, Receive, Scope, Send
+
+from litellm.proxy.common_utils.openai_error_payload import LITELLM_CALL_ID_HEADER
+
+LITELLM_TRACE_ID_HEADER: Final = "x-litellm-trace-id"
+CALL_ID_SPAN_ATTRIBUTE: Final = "litellm.call_id"
+_TRACE_ID_STATE_KEY: Final = "litellm_trace_id"
+_ROOT_SPAN_STATE_KEY: Final = "litellm_trace_root_span"
+# opentelemetry is an optional proxy dependency; resolve it once instead of
+# paying a failed import on every request when it is absent.
+_OTEL_AVAILABLE: Final = find_spec("opentelemetry") is not None
+
+
+def _recording_trace_id(span: object) -> str | None:
+    """The 32-char lowercase W3C trace ID of a recording span with a valid context."""
+    if not _OTEL_AVAILABLE:
+        return None
+    from opentelemetry.trace import Span, format_trace_id
+
+    if not isinstance(span, Span) or not span.is_recording():
+        return None
+    ctx: Final = span.get_span_context()
+    return format_trace_id(ctx.trace_id) if ctx.is_valid else None
+
+
+def anchor_request_root_span(state: State, span: object) -> None:
+    """Remember ``span`` as the request's root span if it records and none is anchored yet."""
+    if getattr(state, _TRACE_ID_STATE_KEY, None) is not None:
+        return
+    trace_id: Final = _recording_trace_id(span)
+    if trace_id is None:
+        return
+    setattr(state, _TRACE_ID_STATE_KEY, trace_id)
+    setattr(state, _ROOT_SPAN_STATE_KEY, span)
+
+
+def request_trace_id(state: State) -> str | None:
+    trace_id: Final = getattr(state, _TRACE_ID_STATE_KEY, None)
+    return trace_id if isinstance(trace_id, str) else None
+
+
+def set_call_id_on_root_span(span: object, call_id: str | None) -> None:
+    """Stamp ``litellm.call_id`` onto a still-recording root span."""
+    if not call_id or not _OTEL_AVAILABLE:
+        return
+    from opentelemetry.trace import Span
+
+    if not isinstance(span, Span) or not span.is_recording():
+        return
+    span.set_attribute(CALL_ID_SPAN_ATTRIBUTE, call_id)
+
+
+def response_trace_id(state: State, call_id: str | None) -> str | None:
+    """The ``x-litellm-trace-id`` value for a response, tying its call ID to the root span."""
+    trace_id: Final = request_trace_id(state)
+    if trace_id is not None:
+        set_call_id_on_root_span(getattr(state, _ROOT_SPAN_STATE_KEY, None), call_id)
+    return trace_id
+
+
+def with_trace_id_header(state: State, response: Response) -> Response:
+    """``response`` carrying ``x-litellm-trace-id``, for responses built outside this middleware."""
+    headers: Final = response.headers
+    trace_id: Final = response_trace_id(state, headers.get(LITELLM_CALL_ID_HEADER))
+    if trace_id is not None:
+        headers[LITELLM_TRACE_ID_HEADER] = trace_id
+    return response
+
+
+class TraceIdHeaderMiddleware:
+    def __init__(self, app: ASGIApp) -> None:
+        self.app = app
+
+    async def __call__(self, scope: Scope, receive: Receive, send: Send) -> None:
+        if scope["type"] != "http" or not _OTEL_AVAILABLE:
+            await self.app(scope, receive, send)
+            return

+"""``x-litellm-trace-id`` on proxy responses and ``litellm.call_id`` on the root server span.

+the FastAPI OTel instrumentation (so it nests inside the server span) and the
+proxy's real exception handlers are registered.

+from fastapi.testclient import TestClient  # noqa: E402

+from opentelemetry.sdk.trace.export import SimpleSpanProcessor  # noqa: E402

+import litellm.proxy.proxy_server as proxy_server_module  # noqa: E402
+from litellm.integrations.opentelemetry import OpenTelemetry  # noqa: E402
+from litellm.integrations.otel.model.config import is_otel_v2_enabled  # noqa: E402
+from litellm.proxy._types import ProxyException  # noqa: E402
+from litellm.proxy.auth.user_api_key_auth import _ensure_parent_otel_span_on_request_state  # noqa: E402
+from litellm.proxy.middleware.trace_id_header_middleware import TraceIdHeaderMiddleware  # noqa: E402
+from litellm.proxy.proxy_server import (  # noqa: E402
+    openai_exception_handler,
+    otel_request_validation_exception_handler,
+    otel_unhandled_exception_handler,
+)
+
+CALL_ID = "7ac48d62-40a1-44e6-8b50-19da641835a5"
+INCOMING_TRACE_ID = "af353cab815b907430a117c9b97b4d0e"

+    @app.post("/stream")
+    def stream():
+        return StreamingResponse(iter([b"data: 1\n\n"]), headers={"x-litellm-call-id": CALL_ID})
+
+    @app.post("/proxy-error/{code}")
+    def proxy_error(code: int):
+        raise ProxyException(

+        )
+
+    @app.post("/boom")
+    def boom():

+
+    @app.get("/health")
+    def health():
+        return {"ok": True}
+
+    app.add_exception_handler(ProxyException, openai_exception_handler)
+    app.add_exception_handler(RequestValidationError, otel_request_validation_exception_handler)

+
+

+    app, exporter = _app()
+    response = TestClient(app).post(
+        "/v1/chat/completions",

+        headers={"traceparent": f"00-{INCOMING_TRACE_ID}-00f067aa0ba902b7-01"},
+    )

+
+

+    app, _ = _app(instrument=False)
+    response = TestClient(app).post("/v1/chat/completions", json={"model": "gpt"})
+    assert response.status_code == 200

+    assert response.headers["x-litellm-call-id"] == CALL_ID
+
+
+def test_header_omitted_when_route_has_no_server_span():
+    app, exporter = _app()
+    response = TestClient(app).get("/health")
+    assert response.status_code == 200
+    assert "x-litellm-trace-id" not in response.headers
+    assert exporter.get_finished_spans() == ()
+
+
+def test_header_omitted_when_server_span_is_sampled_out():
+    from opentelemetry.sdk.trace.sampling import ALWAYS_OFF
+
+    app = FastAPI()
+
+    @app.get("/ping")
+    def ping():
+        return {"ok": True}
+
+    app.add_middleware(TraceIdHeaderMiddleware)
+    FastAPIInstrumentor.instrument_app(app, tracer_provider=TracerProvider(sampler=ALWAYS_OFF))
+    response = TestClient(app).get("/ping")
+    assert response.status_code == 200
+    assert "x-litellm-trace-id" not in response.headers
+
+
+def test_legacy_otel_server_span_trace_id_and_call_id(monkeypatch):
+    """Legacy (non-V2) OTel: the SERVER span is created at auth and ended by the
+    error handler before the response is sent; both values still line up."""
+    monkeypatch.delenv("LITELLM_OTEL_V2", raising=False)
+    is_otel_v2_enabled.cache_clear()
+    exporter = InMemorySpanExporter()
+    provider = TracerProvider()
+    provider.add_span_processor(SimpleSpanProcessor(exporter))
+    otel = OpenTelemetry()
+    otel.tracer = provider.get_tracer("trace-id-header-tests")
+    monkeypatch.setattr(proxy_server_module, "open_telemetry_logger", otel)
+
+    app = FastAPI()
+
+    @app.post("/v1/chat/completions")
+    def chat(request: Request):
+        _ensure_parent_otel_span_on_request_state(request)
+        raise ProxyException(
+            message="bad model",
+            type="invalid_request_error",
+            param=None,
+            code=400,
+            headers={"x-litellm-call-id": CALL_ID},
+        )
+
+    app.add_exception_handler(ProxyException, openai_exception_handler)
+    app.add_middleware(TraceIdHeaderMiddleware)
+
+    response = TestClient(app).post(
+        "/v1/chat/completions", headers={"traceparent": f"00-{INCOMING_TRACE_ID}-00f067aa0ba902b7-01"}
+    )
+    is_otel_v2_enabled.cache_clear()
+
+    assert response.status_code == 400
+    assert response.headers["x-litellm-trace-id"] == INCOMING_TRACE_ID
+    assert response.headers["x-litellm-call-id"] == CALL_ID
+    assert (_server_span(exporter).attributes or {})["litellm.call_id"] == CALL_ID
+
+
+def test_proxy_app_nests_trace_middleware_inside_otel_server_span():
+    middleware = [m.cls for m in proxy_server_module.app.user_middleware]
+    assert TraceIdHeaderMiddleware in middleware
+    if OpenTelemetryMiddleware in middleware:
+        # user_middleware is listed outermost first.
+        assert middleware.index(TraceIdHeaderMiddleware) > middleware.index(OpenTelemetryMiddleware)

+    claim_server_span(span)
+    propagator: Final = get_global_response_propagator()  # pyright: ignore[reportUnknownVariableType]  # upstream leaves inject unannotated
+    if propagator is None:
+        return MappingProxyType({})
+    start: Final[dict[str, object]] = {"type": "http.response.start"}  # mutable-ok: the propagator writes into it
+    propagator.inject(start, context=trace.set_span_in_context(span), setter=asgi_setter)  # pyright: ignore[reportUnknownMemberType]  # upstream leaves inject unannotated
+    return MappingProxyType({key: ", ".join(asgi_getter.get(start, key) or ()) for key in asgi_getter.keys(start)})  # pyright: ignore[reportUnknownMemberType]  # the ASGI instrumentation ships no py.typed marker

+from contextvars import ContextVar
+from typing import Final
+
+from opentelemetry import trace
+from opentelemetry.context import Context
+from opentelemetry.instrumentation.asgi import (  # pyright: ignore[reportMissingTypeStubs]  # the ASGI instrumentation ships no py.typed marker
+    asgi_getter,
+)
+from opentelemetry.instrumentation.propagators import ResponsePropagator
+from opentelemetry.propagators.textmap import CarrierT, Setter, default_setter
+from opentelemetry.trace import Span, format_span_id, format_trace_id
+from opentelemetry.trace.propagation.tracecontext import TraceContextTextMapPropagator
+
+from litellm.integrations.otel.model.semconv import LiteLLM
+
+_LITELLM_SERVER_SPAN: Final[ContextVar[Span | None]] = ContextVar(
+    "litellm_otel_traceresponse_server_span", default=None
+)
+
+
+def claim_server_span(span: Span) -> None:
+    _LITELLM_SERVER_SPAN.set(span)
+
+
+def _response_header(message: dict[str, object], name: str) -> str | None:  # mutable-ok: asgi_getter takes a dict
+    values: Final = asgi_getter.get(message, name)  # pyright: ignore[reportUnknownMemberType]  # the ASGI instrumentation ships no py.typed marker
+    return values[0] if values else None
+
+
+def _http_response_start(message: object) -> dict[str, object] | None:  # mutable-ok: the propagator writes into it
+    if isinstance(message, dict) and message.get("type") == "http.response.start":  # pyright: ignore[reportUnknownMemberType]  # an ASGI message is an untyped dict
+        return message  # pyright: ignore[reportUnknownVariableType]  # an ASGI message is an untyped dict
+    return None
+
+
+def _link_a_restarted_upstream_trace(span: Span, upstream_traceresponse: str) -> None:
+    upstream: Final = trace.get_current_span(
+        TraceContextTextMapPropagator().extract({"traceparent": upstream_traceresponse})
+    ).get_span_context()
+    if upstream.trace_id != span.get_span_context().trace_id:
+        span.add_link(upstream)
+
+
+class UpstreamFirstTraceResponsePropagator(ResponsePropagator):
+    def inject(
+        self,
+        carrier: CarrierT,
+        context: Context | None = None,
+        setter: Setter[CarrierT] = default_setter,
+    ) -> None:
+        start: Final = _http_response_start(carrier)
+        if start is None:
+            return
+        span: Final = trace.get_current_span(context)
+        if span is not _LITELLM_SERVER_SPAN.get():
+            return
+        call_id: Final = _response_header(start, "x-litellm-call-id")
+        if call_id:
+            span.set_attribute(LiteLLM.CALL_ID, call_id)
+        upstream_traceresponse: Final = _response_header(start, "traceresponse")
+        if upstream_traceresponse is not None:
+            _link_a_restarted_upstream_trace(span, upstream_traceresponse)
+            return
+        own: Final = span.get_span_context()
+        if not own.trace_flags.sampled:
+            return
+        sent: Final = start.get("headers")
+        if isinstance(sent, tuple):
+            start["headers"] = [*sent]
+        setter.set(
+            carrier,
+            "traceresponse",
+            f"00-{format_trace_id(own.trace_id)}-{format_span_id(own.span_id)}-{own.trace_flags:02x}",
+        )

+MARKER: Final = re.compile(rb"traceresp-[0-9a-f]{32}")
+TRACERESPONSE: Final = re.compile(r"00-([0-9a-f]{32})-([0-9a-f]{16})-01")
+SERVER: Final = 2
+CALL_ID: Final = "litellm.call_id"
+ANSWER: Final = "trace ok"
+JSON_OBJECT: Final = TypeAdapter(dict[str, JsonValue])
+UPSTREAM_CALL_ID: Final = "upstream-chosen-call-id"
+HOSTILE_UPSTREAM_VALUES: Final = MappingProxyType(
+    {
+        "empty": "",
+        "numeric": "12345",
+        "big": "00-" + "a" * 5000,
+        "garbage": "not-a-traceparent",
+        "joined": f"00-{'1' * 32}-{'2' * 16}-01, 00-{'3' * 32}-{'4' * 16}-01",
+    }
+)
+RELAY_CASES: Final = ("none", "continued", "restarted", "callid", *HOSTILE_UPSTREAM_VALUES)

+def _marker() -> str:

+

+def _trace_id() -> str:

+def _chat_reply(identity: str, stream: bool) -> Reply:
+    message: Final = {"role": "assistant", "content": ANSWER}
+    usage: Final = {"prompt_tokens": 7, "completion_tokens": 2, "total_tokens": 9}
+    if not stream:
+        return Reply(
+            body=json.dumps(
+                {
+                    "id": identity,
+                    "object": "chat.completion",
+                    "created": 1,
+                    "model": "gpt-4o-mini",
+                    "choices": [{"index": 0, "message": message, "finish_reason": "stop"}],
+                    "usage": usage,
+                }
+            ).encode()
+        )
+    chunk: Final = {"id": identity, "object": "chat.completion.chunk", "created": 1, "model": "gpt-4o-mini"}
+    frames: Final = (
+        {**chunk, "choices": [{"index": 0, "delta": message}]},
+        {**chunk, "choices": [{"index": 0, "delta": {}, "finish_reason": "stop"}], "usage": usage},
+    )
+    return Reply(
+        content_type="text/event-stream",
+        chunks=(*(b"data: " + json.dumps(frame).encode() + b"\n\n" for frame in frames), b"data: [DONE]\n\n"),
+    )
+
+
+def _responses_reply(identity: str, stream: bool) -> Reply:
+    response: Final = {
+        "id": identity,
+        "object": "response",
+        "created_at": 1,
+        "status": "completed",
+        "model": "gpt-4o-mini",
+        "output": [
+            {
+                "id": "msg_" + identity,
+                "type": "message",
+                "role": "assistant",
+                "status": "completed",
+                "content": [{"type": "output_text", "text": ANSWER, "annotations": []}],
+            }
+        ],
+        "usage": {"input_tokens": 7, "output_tokens": 2, "total_tokens": 9},
+    }
+    if not stream:
+        return Reply(body=json.dumps(response).encode())
+    events: Final = (
+        {"type": "response.created", "sequence_number": 0, "response": {**response, "status": "in_progress"}},
+        {
+            "type": "response.output_text.delta",
+            "sequence_number": 1,
+            "item_id": "msg_" + identity,
+            "output_index": 0,
+            "content_index": 0,
+            "delta": ANSWER,
+        },
+        {"type": "response.completed", "sequence_number": 2, "response": response},
+    )
+    return Reply(
+        content_type="text/event-stream",
+        chunks=tuple(f"event: {event['type']}\ndata: {json.dumps(event)}\n\n".encode() for event in events),
+    )

+
+def _provider(request: Request) -> Reply:
+    found: Final = MARKER.search(request.body)
+    if found is None:
+        return Reply(status=404, body=b'{"error":"no marker"}')
+    marker: Final = found.group(0).decode()
+    stream: Final = JSON_OBJECT.validate_json(request.body).get("stream") is True
+    if request.target.endswith("/responses"):
+        return _responses_reply(f"resp_{marker}", stream)
+    return _chat_reply(f"chatcmpl-{marker}", stream)
+
+
+def _query(request: Request) -> Mapping[str, str]:
+    return MappingProxyType({name: values[0] for name, values in parse_qs(urlsplit(request.target).query).items()})
+
+
+def _continued_traceresponse(request: Request) -> Reply:
+    incoming: Final = TRACERESPONSE.fullmatch(request.headers.get("traceparent", ""))
+    if incoming is None:
+        return Reply(status=400, body=b'{"error":"no sampled traceparent reached the upstream"}')
+    return Reply(body=b'{"case":"continued"}', headers={"traceresponse": f"00-{incoming.group(1)}-{_span_id()}-01"})
+
+
+def _relay(request: Request) -> Reply:
+    case: Final = urlsplit(request.target).path.rsplit("/", 1)[-1]
+    query: Final = _query(request)
+    body: Final = json.dumps({"case": case}).encode()
+    if case == "continued":
+        return _continued_traceresponse(request)
+    if case == "restarted":
+        return Reply(body=body, headers={"traceresponse": f"00-{query['trace']}-{query['span']}-01"})
+    if case == "callid":
+        return Reply(status=int(query.get("status", "200")), body=body, headers={"x-litellm-call-id": UPSTREAM_CALL_ID})
+    if case in HOSTILE_UPSTREAM_VALUES:
+        return Reply(body=body, headers={"traceresponse": HOSTILE_UPSTREAM_VALUES[case]})
+    return Reply(body=body)
+

+@dataclass(frozen=True, slots=True)
+class ExportedSpan:
+    trace_id: str
+    span_id: str
+    parent_span_id: str
+    kind: int
+    attributes: Mapping[str, JsonValue]
+    links: tuple[tuple[str, str], ...]

+def _attribute(value: JsonValue) -> JsonValue:
+    typed: Final = object_value(value)
+    return next((typed[key] for key in ("stringValue", "intValue", "boolValue", "doubleValue") if key in typed), None)
+
+
+def _link(value: JsonValue) -> tuple[str, str]:
+    link: Final = object_value(value)
+    return str(link["traceId"]), str(link["spanId"])
+
+
+def _exported(value: JsonValue) -> ExportedSpan:
+    span: Final = object_value(value)
+    attributes: Final = tuple(object_value(attribute) for attribute in list_value(span.get("attributes", [])))
+    return ExportedSpan(
+        trace_id=str(span["traceId"]),
+        span_id=str(span["spanId"]),
+        parent_span_id=str(span.get("parentSpanId", "")),
+        kind=int(str(span.get("kind", 0))),
+        attributes=MappingProxyType({str(item["key"]): _attribute(item["value"]) for item in attributes}),
+        links=tuple(_link(link) for link in list_value(span.get("links", []))),
+    )
+
+
+def _scope_spans(resource: JsonValue) -> Iterator[JsonValue]:
+    return itertools.chain.from_iterable(
+        list_value(object_value(scope).get("spans", [])) for scope in list_value(object_value(resource)["scopeSpans"])
+    )
+
+
+def _batch_spans(body: bytes) -> tuple[ExportedSpan, ...]:
+    resources: Final = list_value(JSON_OBJECT.validate_json(body).get("resourceSpans", []))
+    return tuple(_exported(span) for span in itertools.chain.from_iterable(map(_scope_spans, resources)))
+

+@dataclass(frozen=True, slots=True)
+class Collector:
+    wire: Wire
+    outage: threading.Event
+    accepted: Sequence[Request]
+    guard: threading.Lock
+
+    def spans(self) -> tuple[ExportedSpan, ...]:
+        with self.guard:
+            batches: Final = tuple(self.accepted)
+        return tuple(itertools.chain.from_iterable(_batch_spans(batch.body) for batch in batches))
+
+    def with_span_id(self, span_id: str) -> tuple[ExportedSpan, ...]:
+        return tuple(span for span in self.spans() if span.span_id == span_id)
+
+    def span(self, span_id: str) -> ExportedSpan:
+        eventually(lambda: self.with_span_id(span_id), lambda found: len(found) >= 1, seconds=30)
+        found: Final = self.with_span_id(span_id)
+        assert len(found) == 1, found
+        return found[0]
+
+    def server_spans_for_call(self, call_id: str) -> tuple[ExportedSpan, ...]:
+        return tuple(span for span in self.spans() if span.kind == SERVER and span.attributes.get(CALL_ID) == call_id)
+
+    def server_span_for_call(self, call_id: str) -> ExportedSpan:
+        eventually(lambda: self.server_spans_for_call(call_id), lambda found: len(found) >= 1, seconds=30)
+        found: Final = self.server_spans_for_call(call_id)
+        assert len(found) == 1, found
+        return found[0]
